items.description: Sec. 4 says 'See Figure 9 for domain sizes'; no dimensions appear in the text. They can only be inferred from Table 2 (60×30 elements, h_c = 1/30, so square elements) as a 2:1 rectangle. The absolute size, the units and the length L used in Sec. 4 are not stated.
readings: 2 × 1 rectangle (length 2, height 1), i.e. 2L × L with L = 1
The same 2:1 rectangle labelled L × L/2 (L = 2) or in other units; only the aspect ratio is kept

items.entity: fixed boundary of the Michell cantilever
items.description: Sec. 4 defers the 'exact placement of boundaries' to Fig. 9a, and Sec. 4.2 only names the 'Michell cantilever beam [35]'. The text never says which edge, which part of it, or whether a circular support (as in Michell's classical problem) is fixed.
readings: Entire left edge, x = 0, y in [0, H]
Only a central segment of the left edge, e.g. y in [0.25H, 0.75H]
Circular/semicircular fixed support centred at mid-height on the left side (classical Michell cantilever)

items.entity: restraint type on the fixed boundary
items.description: The text never says whether the support restrains both displacement components or only one; this is shown only in Fig. 9a.
readings: Fully clamped: u_x = u_y = 0 at all support nodes
Roller-type: u_x = 0 along the support, with u_y = 0 at one node only (e.g. mid-height)

items.description: Sec. 4 defers load placement to Fig. 9a. The text gives only the length of the loaded line (1/10 L), not which edge it is on or at what height.
readings: Right edge (x = 2), segment centred at mid-height y = 0.5H
Right edge, segment at the bottom-right corner (from y = 0 to y = L/10)
Right edge, segment at the top-right corner (from y = H - L/10 to y = H)

items.description: The force direction appears only in Fig. 9a. For a single load case the sign (up or down) does not change the optimum, but a transverse versus an axial load does.
readings: Vertical (transverse) force, e.g. -y
Horizontal (axial) force, +/-x

items.entity: length of the loaded line ('1/10 L')
items.description: Sec. 4: 'the force is applied along a line of 1/10 L in the Michell cantilever case'. L is never defined in the text (only in Fig. 9). For the inferred 2×1 domain, L could be the height or the length.
readings: L = height = 1, so the loaded length is 0.1 (3 elements on 60×30, 12 on 240×120, 72 on 1440×720)
L = length = 2, so the loaded length is 0.2 (6 elements on 60×30)

items.entity: distribution of the force over the loaded line
items.description: Sec. 4 does not say how the force is spread along the 1/10 L line: as a uniform traction or as equal nodal forces.
readings: Uniform traction on a boundary segment (consistent nodal loads, half weight at the segment ends)
Equal point forces on every node of the segment

items.description: No force value is given anywhere. The tabulated compliances (C_ref about 106 at V about 0.25) suggest a unit load and unit modulus, but the text does not say so.
readings: Total force F = 1
Unit traction (force per unit length = 1, so the total equals the loaded length)
F = 1 at each loaded node

items.description: The captions of Figs. 10-12 give V = 0.25 and V = 0.40. Table 2 lists V_ref = 0.2535/0.2568/0.2614 and 0.4024/0.4080/0.4165 for mu_min = 0.05/0.10/0.20, with slightly different values in Table 3 and App. A. Eq. (1) applies V_max to rho^d, whose superscript is never defined, so the bound actually imposed is not stated.
readings: V* = 0.25 and V* = 0.40 (nominal values from the captions)
V* = V_f of the de-homogenized design being compared (e.g. 0.2695, 0.4329)

items.description: Sec. 4: 'all elements with a density of rho>0.99 and in a small radius around the load are set to solid'. The radius is not given. It is unclear whether this is a passive solid region during optimization or only a post-processing step, and whether 'and' means union or intersection.
readings: No passive region in the optimization (solidification only in post-processing)
Passive solid disc at the load with radius about L/20 (about 0.05)
Passive solid disc at the load with radius about L/10 (about 0.1)
Passive solid patch of 1-2 coarse elements (about 0.03-0.07) around the loaded nodes

items.description: Neither E nor the thickness is given. Only the relative void stiffness alpha_out = 1e-9 is stated (Sec. 2.1.1).
readings: E = 1 and thickness = 1 (dimensionless)
Physical values, e.g. E = 210 GPa, t = 1 mm

items.entity: Poisson's ratio of the base material
items.description: The Poisson's ratio is never stated.
The text does not say whether the 2D linear-elastic analysis uses plane stress or plane strain. Plane strain changes the effective Poisson ratio.
readings: Plane stress
Plane strain

items.entity: analysis mesh for the single-material re-run
items.description: Sec. 4.2 uses homogenization meshes 60×30 (Table 2), 240×120 (Table 3) and 120×60 (App. A), and fine meshes 1440×720, 2400×1200, 2880×1440 and 5760×2880. Sec. 4.2.1 times top88 at 1440×720 and 2400×1200. The text does not say which resolution defines the single-material problem.

Sec. 4 gives 'a filter radius of r_min=1.2 for varying mesh sizes' without units. It is stated only for the coarse homogenization meshes, with nothing on how it carries over to a finer single-material mesh.
readings: 1.2 times the element size of whatever mesh is used
Fixed physical radius 1.2·h_c of the 60×30 mesh = 0.04 (about 28.8 elements on 1440×720, 48 on 2400×1200)
Fixed physical radius 1.2·h_c of the 240×120 mesh = 0.01 (about 7.2 elements on 1440×720)

items.description: Eq. (2) says only that the variables are 'filtered'. The filter type (density, sensitivity or PDE) and its weight function are not given.
readings: Density filter with linear cone weights
Sensitivity filter
PDE (Helmholtz) filter

items.description: Eqs. (1)-(4) use projected variables with superscripts k, e and d, which look like the eroded/dilated realizations of Giele et al. [15]. The sharpness beta, the thresholds eta and any continuation are not given, and the volume constraint is applied to rho^d.
readings: No projection (use the filtered field directly)
Single Heaviside projection, eta = 0.5, with beta continuation (e.g. 1 to 32)
Robust formulation with eroded/intermediate/dilated thresholds (e.g. 0.75/0.5/0.25) and the volume constraint on the dilated field

items.entity: material interpolation / penalization for the single-material solver
items.description: The reference solutions use unpenalized rank-2 homogenization. Sec. 4.2.1 says a single-material (top88) run needs 'a continuation strategy ... around 1000 iterations' but gives no penalization exponent or schedule.
readings: SIMP p = 3 fixed, E_min = 1e-9·E
SIMP with continuation p = 1 to 3 (or higher) over about 1000 iterations
No penalization (p = 1, grey variable-thickness design)

items.entity: optimizer, initial design and stopping criterion
items.description: Sec. 4 says only that the problem is 'solved until convergence'. No optimizer, initial design, tolerance or iteration limit is given; Sec. 4.2.1 mentions only about 1000 iterations.
readings: MMA, uniform start at V*, stop when the maximum design change is below 0.01
OC (top88), uniform start, fixed at about 1000 iterations
MMA, stop when the relative objective change is below 1e-4 or at an iteration cap (e.g. 500)

items.entity: objective normalization C_ref and solid-area penalty Gamma
items.description: Eq. (1) divides the compliance by C_ref and adds Gamma·V_struct(s)/V_Omega with Gamma = 0.05. C_ref is never given a value, so the weight of the penalty is unknown. It is also unclear whether this term and the s field should be kept in a single-material re-run.
readings: Omit the Gamma term (plain volume-constrained compliance)
Keep Gamma = 0.05 with C_ref = compliance of the initial uniform design
Keep Gamma = 0.05 with C_ref = 1

items.description: Tables 2-3 and Figs. 10-12 vary mu_min, the lower bound on the lamination parameters in eq. (1). The text gives no equivalent length scale for a single-material density solver, so it is undetermined how the three mu_min cases should differ in a re-run.
readings: Ignore mu_min (one problem per volume fraction)
Impose a minimum member width of about mu_min·eps_f (3/6/12 h_f for eps_f = 60h_f; 2.5/5/10 h_f for eps_f = 50h_f) using robust or length-scale control
Reflect mu_min only through the case-specific V_ref values of Table 2 as volume limits
